candidates.label: Illyricum (Roman province, label point)
candidates.support: Identified with the Roman province along the eastern Adriatic, governed from Salona. The label point is Wikidata's point for the province, about 65 km from Pleiades' independent point for the same province under its later name, 'Dalmatia.'

summary.text: Illyricum was a Roman province along the eastern shore of the Adriatic Sea. Paul writes to the Romans that he has 'fully preached the Good News of Christ' from Jerusalem 'all the way around to Illyricum,' and he later reports sending Titus 'to Dalmatia.' The International Standard Bible Encyclopedia treats these as the same province under two names, one earlier and one later.

history.text: The International Standard Bible Encyclopedia records that the province Paul calls Illyricum in its 'narrower and more precise' sense was 'finally organized' by Augustus, and that it 'later came to be known as Dalmatia,' citing Tacitus's Annals, Josephus's Jewish War, and Cassius Dio as ancient authorities who use the name Dalmatia for the same province. The companion International Standard Bible Encyclopedia article on Dalmatia agrees that Paul's use of that name in 2 Timothy 4:10 'most probably' refers to the whole province, the same one named Illyricum in Romans 15:19.

The province was governed by an imperial legate residing at Salona, on the Dalmatian coast, and the International Standard Bible Encyclopedia dates Paul's own travel toward its frontier, described in Romans 15:19, to his third missionary journey, during his second visit to Macedonia.

scripture.textWEB: in the power of signs and wonders, in the power of God’s Spirit; so that from Jerusalem and around as far as to Illyricum, I have fully preached the Good News of Christ;
for Demas left me, having loved this present world, and went to Thessalonica; Crescens to Galatia; and Titus to Dalmatia.
